Jordan Spieth. An American professional golfer who won 3 major championships and emerged as one of the sport's brightest young talents in the 2010s. Known for his short-game brilliance and aggressive style, he represented a new generation of golfers competing at the highest levels of the sport.

He won 3 major championships: 2 Masters in 2015 and 2022, 1 US Open in 2015, and 1 Open Championship in 2017. In 2015, he won the Masters and US Open in the same calendar year as a 21-year-old, establishing himself as an elite talent. Spieth was known for his exceptional chipping and short-game creativity, skills that distinguished him from peers. He captured the attention of American golf fans as a homegrown star with competitive intensity and dedication.

He won 13 PGA Tour events and numerous international tournaments during his career. Competing professionally from 2013 onward, he established himself as one of the most significant American golfers of the 2010s generation. He demonstrated remarkable consistency in major championships despite periods of competitive struggle and self-doubt. Rory McIlroy was a contemporary competitor from the same generational cohort. Tiger Woods inspired and influenced Spieth's competitive approach, and Phil Mickelson was a predecessor who mentored and influenced Spieth during his rise.
